analysis.cultural_economic_read: A serviced but modest inland African town: tarred trunk road with streetlighting and electrification, but sand shoulders, hand-painted shopfronts, PO-box addressing and mixed rondavel/block-house homesteads. Economy is highway-service and informal retail (bottle store, phone/airtime shop, tyre and car-wash businesses, cement-block yard), plus a public vocational 'Brigade' training centre — a Botswana state-supported skills institution. Anglophone signage over a Setswana-speaking population; school uniforms indicate functioning public education. Middle-income southern African standard of living with visible dry-season subsistence landscape.

narrative.blind_logic: The blind chain relies entirely on street-level visual cues: vegetation/soil type, hand-painted signage in Setswana/English, brand names (St Louis Lager, Orange airtime), architecture (rondavels, lolwapa compounds), and infrastructure density (tarred road, streetlights, Brigade institution sign) to progressively narrow from continent to a peripheral ward of Mahalapye. Its finest-grained step (district/ward) is inferred from comparing shopfront formality and building types against an imagined CBD, all still grounded in what's visible in the panel. No external toponyms or coordinates are used — the Brigade sign itself supplies the town name directly from imagery.
narrative.aided_logic: The aided chain follows an identical evidentiary path through country and macro-region (same signage, brands, vegetation cues), but at the admin_region and district steps it explicitly invokes the map overlay's toponyms — Borotsi, Boseja, Dilaene wards, Tamocha School, Mahalapye River — and states the marker's plotted position relative to the A1 and river to decide 'western Mahalapye wards, Borotsi/Tamocha strip.' The final ward-level claim is justified by where the red marker sits on the map, not by any distinguishing street-level feature.
narrative.delta: Through country/macro_region the two chains are essentially identical, using the same brand, language, and vegetation discriminators. The divergence begins at admin_region and sharpens at district: the aided chain introduces ward names (Borotsi, Boseja, Dilaene) and a school/river toponymy that could only come from reading the map panel, not from the street-view images. The final west-of-A1/Borotsi-Tamocha localization is justified by marker position relative to labeled features, effectively reading the answer off the map rather than inferring it from visual evidence — the discriminators here ('marker sits west of A1 shield') are post-hoc rationalizations anchored to the marker, not independent street-level proof.
